title: Brieskorn links: ES solutions never give integral homology spheres
connection: The link of x^a + y^b + z^c is an integral homology sphere iff a, b, c are pairwise coprime. Pairwise coprime ES solutions are impossible (constraint-world item), so ES links always have non-trivial H₁.

avenue.role: calibration only (topology of Brieskorn links of ES triples)

Hence every ES Brieskorn link has non-trivial H₁ (its torsion is the gcd skeleton of the solution).

record.summary: Type I divisor condition (f | p² + 4c²d, f ≡ −p mod 4cd) for 211 primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 below 3000, c ≤ 20, d ≤ 30: no solution ever occurs with d = 1 (0 of 211), and some solution exists for every prime with d ≤ 30 (smallest d: 2 in 110 cases, 3 in 34, 5 in 32, 6 in 10). The residue condition is therefore a genus condition in Q(√−d), as the item suspected, and d = 1 is obstructed for all p ≡ 1 (mod 4).

title: Binary quadratic forms: Type I as representation of p² by a form of discriminant −16c²d

Equivalently, (p, c·2√(−d)) is a vector in an imaginary quadratic order; the norm factorisation is governed by the class group of ℚ(√−d).

title: Inverse Littlewood–Offord for I3 at fixed t: walks in (ℤ/t)^×
connection: For I3 at fixed t, success needs a divisor of tn+1 ≡ −1 (mod t) — a signed subset-product hitting −1 in (ℤ/t)^× (t small!).

avenue.role: I3 at fixed small level t: signed subset products of the prime factors of tn + 1 hitting −1 in a tiny group (ℤ/t)^× (local-limit/Littlewood–Offord)

With T growing (T = (log n)^A), it is a bounded-window statement in the forbidden (polylog) regime for both endpoints ('H4_NOT_POLYLOG': witnesses with both endpoints ≤ (log p)^C are false i.o., unconditionally). For the chain lattice, w has coordinates (v,t,u) mod 2 and w² has denominator p. This plausibly yields (A/p) as a function of p mod 8 and the parity pattern of (t,u,v,tu−1,tv−1), i.e. the slot lemma.

avenue.missing_theorem: None for ES. PROVED here (3-adic valuation, elementary): an Eisenstein norm is 3^k·m with m ≡ 1 (mod 3). If 4/p = Σ 1/(3^{k_i} m_i) then all three k_i are equal to some K ≥ 1 and v₃(Σ 1/m_i) = K. A unique minimal k or a pair at minimal k gives v₃ < 0, and all k_i = 0 gives v₃ ≥ 1. title: Check whether Type II with c ≥ 2 is itself just the C-form for a *composite* n: ff′ = 4c²dp + 1 with f ≡ f′ ≡ −1 (mod 4cd) ⟺ C-form certificate for n = cp with C = cd?
connection: C-form for n' = cp with C' = cd: 4C'n' + 1 = 4cd·cp + 1 = 4c²dp + 1 ✓ and a ≡ b ≡ −1 mod 4C' = 4cd ✓. So Type II for p with parameters (c, d) is EXACTLY the C-form for the multiple n = cp with parameter C = cd. Hence: ES(p) via Type II ⟺ some multiple cp of p has a C-form certificate; and a solution for cp gives one for p by scaling?? NO — scaling goes the other way (solution for n gives one for multiples). Hmm: C-form for cp gives 4/(cp) = 1/(C'uv) + 1/(cpC'v) + 1/(cpC'u) ⟹ multiply by c: 4/p = c/(C'uv) + 1/(pC'v) + 1/(pC'u) — first term c/(cd·uv) = 1/(duv) ✓ a unit fraction! So yes: a C-form certificate for cp with C' = cd yields 4/p = 1/(duv) + 1/(pcdv) + 1/(pcdu). Consistent. So full Type II ⟺ 'some multiple cp of p, with C a multiple of c, has a C-form certificate' — the slack is exactly 'pass to a multiple'.

record.summary: Janson-type lower-tail bound in a random-residue model for the box {4uB ≤ X} (events p ≡ -(u+B) mod 4uB): mu grows as ≈0.145 (log X)^2 (mu=13.55 at X=16000) while Delta/mu grows ≈0.5 log X (Delta/mu=5.0 at X=16000) because all moduli share the factor 4 and dependence is dense. ES over O_K for real quadratic K: Gal(K/ℚ) acts on K-solutions of 4/p = 1/x+1/y+1/z with totally positive x,y,z; fixed points are ℚ-solutions. If the number of K-solutions in a Galois-stable finite window is odd, a rational solution exists.

Non-rational solutions pair under conjugation, so the K-count ≡ the ℚ-count (mod 2). The missing theorem is therefore the same as 'the ℚ-count in that set is odd', which is ES itself in parity form. Any count-parity theorem must also see the quadratic character, since the Type I/II count is 0 at odd squares (M5 row).

title: p-adic interpolation along exponential families (Skolem–Mahler–Lech)
connection: SML proves zero sets of linear recurrences are periodic + finite via p-adic analytic interpolation. ES along n_s = a·b^s + c: certificate conditions involve divisors of 4C·n_s + 1 = 4Ca·b^s + (4Cc + 1), an exponential sequence; p-adic interpolation of 'divisibility by a fixed d' gives periodic structure in s, possibly proving ES for open families like 15·2^s + 1 by periodic covering + finitely many checks.

avenue.role: thin-family ES via periodic (Skolem–Mahler–Lech) sets in the exponent: finite covering of s for 15·2^s + 1
avenue.missing_theorem: For n_s = 15·2^s + 1 there are finitely many (C,d), d ≡ −1 (mod 4C), whose periodic sets {s : d | 4C·n_s + 1} cover all s ≥ s₀. Fixed (C,d) gives an ET/divisor class in s, and EXPONENT_COVERING Cor 1.5 (PROVED) says k = 15 = 4² − 1 is an integer unit-square obstruction point at μ = 0. So no finite covering of 15·2^s + 1 by ET/divisor classes exists. DEPTH_ASPECT Lemma 1.3 kills the natural exponential-polynomial witness shapes (B1). The families proved so far (3·2^s+1, 63·2^s+1, 7·4^s+9) used forced-budget windows (Aurifeuillean factorisations), not coverings.
avenue.yield: partial (one thin family), if a window mechanism replaces the covering
avenue.status_ref: EXPONENT_COVERING.md Thm 1.4 / Cor 1.5 (PROVED: k = 4^j − 1 points); BRAINSTORM/bsE_padic_interpolation.md (DEPTH_ASPECT Lemma 1.3, COLLAPSES B1); EXP_15.md §2 (F1 menus at μ = 0); FRONTIER §7.8

title: Positivity from an exact divisor-sum formula: where the tail can be bounded
connection: For the partition function, positivity is trivial but Lehmer bounded the Rademacher tail explicitly. ES level counts are exact divisor-class sums (R_t(n) = D_t^−(tn+1) − β_t(n)); summing over t with weights, the 'tail' is the order-≥3 character part X(n). Ask for the explicit size of X(n) relative to M_BM in the exact formula at small levels.

avenue.role: explicit tail bound in the exact formula: X(p)/M_BM(p) stays above −1
avenue.missing_theorem: X(p) ≥ −(1 − ε)M_gen(p) (equivalently R(p) ≥ ε·M_gen(p)) for every large prime p.
avenue.status_ref: This is H⁻_BM in genus form (FRONTIER §2.4: 'ES-(★) in disguise up to ε'); the two-sided version |X| < M_gen is false i.o. (Prop 3.1). Lehmer's Rademacher-tail bound works because the tail is an absolutely convergent explicit series; X(p) is a sum of ≍ p log p order-≥ 3 character terms with no decay.
avenue.next: None. (Plot X/M_BM for p ≤ 10⁷ if data is wanted; at the 14 (★)-failures it is −M_gen/M_BM by definition.)
avenue.note: The exact formula is known (genus split, Thm K); the tail is the problem.

title: Covering-system disproof search on exponential families (Sierpiński-type)
connection: Sierpiński/Erdős obstructions arise when every member of an exponential family is forced to have a small prime factor. For ES families n_s = k·2^s + 1, check whether a covering system could force every certificate condition to fail for all s (it would give infinitely many ES counterexamples).

avenue.role: disproof architecture: Sierpiński-type covering system forcing ES failure along an exponential family
avenue.missing_theorem: A finite covering {s ≡ a_i (mod m_i)} such that for each s in class i every ES certificate of n_s = k·2^s + 1 fails. Impossible in both readings: (a) a Sierpiński covering forces a small prime q_i | n_s, and then ES(n_s) holds by scaling from ES(q_i); (b) a finite covering controls only finitely many slices, while certifying moduli move up to O(n_s²) (B-fin), and emptying a finite slice set is the 'n = 1 shadow' (DISPROOF_AVENUES Prop 3.1), not ES failure.
avenue.yield: none (a disproof would need a 'prime T1')
avenue.status_ref: (a) scaling (FRONTIER §1); (b) DISPROOF_AVENUES.md Prop 3.1 (n = 1 shadow kills any finite slice set, existence CONDITIONAL on Dickson/H), FRONTIER §3 B-fin, §7.15 (prime T1 is the only disproof shape); BRAINSTORM/bsE_sierpinski_moving_integer.md
avenue.next: None for disproof. For the proof side of 15·2^s + 1 the periodic-set computation is (J)102's open branch (FRONTIER §7.8).
avenue.note: Divisibility coverings help ES rather than hurt it — the Sierpiński analogy points the wrong way.

connection: Pell is solvable exactly for non-squares. ES Type I/II fail at all odd squares (T1) and, per the repo, U(n) fails at odd squares plus {105, 2961, 3985, 25305, 111969, 978145}. Formulate the precise 'Pell-shaped' conjecture (Type I ∪ II solvable for every odd non-square n outside an explicit finite list) and treat it as the natural target with the right exception set.

avenue.role: target formulation: 'Pell-shaped' conjecture — Type I ∪ II solvable at every odd non-square outside a finite list
avenue.missing_theorem: CONJECTURE: f_I(n) + f_II(n) ≥ 1 for every odd non-square n > n₀ (with Type I/II in ET's coprime sense). At primes this is ES. On composites it is strictly stronger, and coprimality creates sporadic exceptions (e.g. the z52 note: 3985 has coprime Type I solutions but no coprime five-slot word, so composite exceptions depend on which sub-route is used). As a proof target it is ES plus composite cases. Its value is as the T1-exact statement of the expected truth, like H⁻_BM.

title: Variance-to-mean ratio of R(p) as a quasi-independence diagnostic
connection: Koukoulopoulos–Maynard's key was showing overlaps are small on average (quasi-independence). For ES, the variance of R(p) over primes near X relative to its mean measures overlap; Poisson-like behaviour (ratio ≈ 1 after removing the genus fluctuation) indicates quasi-independent events.

avenue.role: calibration: quasi-independence diagnostic; best possible proof role is a second-moment exceptional-set bound
avenue.missing_theorem: Asymptotic Var_{p∼X}(R(p) − M_BM(p)) ≍ E[R(p)]. Chebyshev would then give #{p ≤ X : R(p) = 0} ≪ π(X)/log²X, which is far weaker than the known E(N) ≪ N exp(−c(log N)^{3/4}).
avenue.status_ref: FRONTIER §2.4 zero law (P(R* = 0 | M) is 1.5–2.8× swap-Poisson); (J)103 §3 (fixed-p variance is critical); FRONTIER §6 'Fixed-p variance / Janson → critical'
avenue.barrier: B6 (variance over p is an average)
avenue.next: None as a lane; the measurement is in (J)103.
avenue.note: Overdispersion, not Poisson, is what the repo data show; quasi-independence in KM's sense is a statement about averages.

connection: Bhargava classified universal quadratic forms by finite criteria. For the cubic family F(t,u,v) = a·tuv − b·u − c·v + d with lower bounds on t, u, v, classify which members represent every large integer (I3 is the member a = b = c = 1, d = 0, bounds ≥ 3) and find the nearest universal member to ES's constrained form.
